content:
When Apple finally responded to the dramatic surge in memory and other component costs, it showed no mercy. Some price increases exceeded 50%, with certain memory and storage upgrades even doubling in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come down...

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would lower prices even after component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of readers indicated they expected the price hikes to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing will not see any improvement before 2028, and even then the situation will be limited. It is now quite clear that the current extremely high pricing will remain for at least several years, and is likely never to return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Reduce the quantity or frequency of your Apple purchases? Or take other approaches, such as choosing lower-tier models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?

Please participate in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your consumption behaviour in more than one way.
